sources.why: The repo this one forked from. These are the skills worth tracking upstream rather than owning — see docs/adr/0001.

skills.name: code-review
skills.why: Reviews changes since a fixed point on two axes — repo standards and the originating spec.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.why: Deep-module vocabulary. Shared dependency of grilling and the owned arch-review.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.why: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.why: Maintains ubiquitous language (GLOSSARY.md) and ADRs. Called by arch-review when a term or a load-bearing decision comes up.

skills.name: grilling
skills.why: The interview engine. Model-invoked, so it fires on 'grill me' on its own; used to stress-test plans, often with 'answer with your recommendations'.

skills.name: pr
skills.why: PR body template — diagram, before/after evidence, merge danger. Fills the step before address-review-findings; most PRs here are opened by an agent.

skills.name: research
skills.why: Delegates reading legwork to a background agent and lands findings as Markdown in the repo.

skills.name: tdd
skills.why: Red → green at agreed seams, with what a test worth keeping looks like. Model-invoked; needs only codebase-design and code-review, both curated.

skills.name: wizard
skills.why: Generates a bash wizard for steps only a human can do — dashboard clicks, secrets into .env and gh — with WSL-aware URL opening. Fits the Cloudflare/GitHub setup chores that come up per project.

archived.name: improve-codebase-architecture
archived.why: Replaced by the owned arch-review skill (docs/adr/0004), which adapts its scan and candidate format but writes the backlog into the repo and implements it. User-invoked, so nothing could call it; it stopped after a /tmp report every time.
